repair_notes.uniform_estimate: Fix mu>0, T<infinity, finite nonempty X, and nested Lambda_m containing Lambda_n containing X. With M,R common to the path and kappa_* = sup_s sup_x sum_{S containing x} ||Phi_s(S)|| <= sup_s ||Phi_s||_{F_a}, lem-qsm-boundary-dynamics-cauchy gives sup_{s in [0,1], |t|<=T} ||tau_t^{Lambda_m,Phi_s}(A_s)-tau_t^{Lambda_n,Phi_s}(A_s)|| <= 2 kappa_* |X| (sup_s ||A_s||) T exp(2 kappa_* M exp(mu R) T + mu R) sum_{y outside Lambda_n} exp(-mu dist_infinity(X,{y})), in the stipulated hbar=1 units. This applies directly to A_s=Phi_s\'(Y), X=Y. The derivative is continuous on [0,1], hence bounded for each fixed Y. The nonnegative lattice tail is summable and tends to zero independently of s. No continuity of the entire path in a global interaction Banach norm is needed for this estimate.
repair_notes.filtered_limit: The compact-time Cauchy bound is multiplied by the finite integral of |W_gamma|. For |t|>T the difference between two filtered integrands integrates to at most 2 sup_s ||Phi_s\'(Y)|| times integral_{|t|>T}|W_gamma(t)|dt. First choosing T and then n gives a uniformly Cauchy sequence of filtered terms. Once the neighborhood of a fixed nonempty Z is contained in Lambda_n, only Y subset Z and k<=diam(Z) can have Y_k intersect Lambda_n=Z, leaving finitely many fixed expectation projections. The finite-sum limit gives Psi_infinity(Z,s); finite partial sums of coefficient norms preserve the uniform F_rho bound.
